items.headline: Two Singapore-listed palm oil firms named in a Greenpeace report on Indonesian plantation fires
items.summary: A Greenpeace report linked two Singapore-listed palm oil companies to plantation fires fuelling the transboundary haze; shares of both firms fell when trading opened on 16 October as scrutiny of corporate accountability grew.

items.headline: Borneo residents take the Indonesian government to court over the fires driving the haze
items.summary: Residents of Indonesian Borneo filed a lawsuit accusing the government of negligence in handling the forest fires that have pushed smoke haze across the region, as Singapore's air stayed in the unhealthy range.

items.headline: Seah Kian Peng and Pritam Singh lead a parliamentary delegation to Europe
items.summary: Speaker Seah Kian Peng and Workers' Party chief Pritam Singh are leading a cross-party parliamentary delegation to Vatican City, Italy and France, aimed at strengthening inter-parliamentary ties.

items.headline: SportSG shuts outdoor and non-air-conditioned facilities at all ActiveSG centres as haze persists
items.summary: Sport Singapore closed outdoor and non-air-conditioned facilities at every ActiveSG Sport Centre as a precaution while the haze lingered, with indoor air-conditioned facilities staying open.

items.headline: At least 19 killed in a Durga Puja pandal stampede in Kolkata
items.summary: A crowd rushing for cover from rain at a Durga Puja pavilion in Kolkata triggered a stampede on 17 October that killed at least 19 people, including a seven-year-old girl, and injured 25; police detained organisers and opened a crowd-control probe.

items.headline: Update: India frees 'Cockroach' party founder as voter-roll protests spread
items.summary: Police released Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on 17 October, a day after detaining him en route to a Delhi rally, and his legal team said two more jailed leaders were set to be freed, as demands for the Chief Election Commissioner to resign over a voter-roll purge intensified.

items.headline: Marco Rubio's India visit, centred on Mumbai, ruffles feathers in New Delhi
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's trip to India, focused on Mumbai and skipping New Delhi, drew unease in the capital as ties strain over tariffs and purchases of Russian oil; the State Department said he would meet officials and business leaders on energy and strategic cooperation.

items.headline: Police rule out a criminal probe into a Palestine Action post by an adviser's wife
items.summary: The Metropolitan Police said a social-media post by writer Sarah Helm, wife of national security adviser Jonathan Powell, expressing support for the banned group Palestine Action did not meet the criminal threshold, so no investigation would follow.

items.headline: Green Party member reports death threats over a conference motion on Zionism
items.summary: Green Party member Lubna Speitan said she had received death and rape threats after the party's Brighton conference passed a motion, by 1,022 votes to 813, classing Zionism as a form of racism; Prime Minister Andy Burnham called the motion 'wrong' and ruled out any pact with the Greens.

items.headline: Ukraine launches one of its largest drone attacks of the year on Russia
items.summary: Ukraine struck a St Petersburg oil terminal in one of its biggest drone assaults of 2026, defying US pressure to halt attacks on Russian energy sites; Russia said it downed more than 1,000 drones overnight into 18 October and at least one person was killed.

items.headline: Trump endorses Netanyahu nine days before Israel's election
items.summary: President Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu on 18 October, nine days before Israel's 27 October parliamentary election, reversing an earlier refusal to back him as the prime minister faces a tight race.

items.headline: Fighting intensifies across Yemen as a humanitarian crisis deepens
items.summary: Escalating fighting across Yemen has displaced more than 233,000 people since the latest surge, the International Organization for Migration said, with about 121,000 uprooted in Taiz governorate alone.

items.headline: Ukraine targets Russia's Yandex as the internet becomes a new front line
items.summary: Ukraine said it hit a data centre tied to Yandex, often called 'Russia's Google', signalling a shift toward striking the digital infrastructure that underpins Russia's economy and daily life.

items.headline: Anthropic plans to move 5% of its equity into a new public-good fund ahead of an IPO
items.summary: Anthropic said it would shift about 5% of its shares into a new public-benefit fund that can finance donations addressing issues such as AI's labour-market impact, as the company prepares a November IPO that could value it at up to roughly US$2 trillion.

items.headline: Rivian moves to license its software, AI and autonomy stack
items.summary: Rivian said it would open up its electric-vehicle architecture, AI models and self-driving stack for licensing, while a venture it partly owns, Mind Robotics, builds industrial robots for its factories and outside customers.

items.headline: Waymo's robotaxis are heading to Canada
items.summary: Waymo said it would enter Toronto through Ontario's automated-vehicle pilot programme, first mapping and testing with safety operators on board before carrying passengers, in its first move outside the United States.

items.headline: Eight US states sue OpenAI over ChatGPT child-safety claims
items.summary: Attorneys general in eight states - Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana - filed separate lawsuits alleging ChatGPT is a defective product that has harmed children; OpenAI said its tools include age-specific protections 'many other AI products lack'.

items.headline: Brent crude tops US$110 for the first time since May
items.summary: Brent crude touched US$110 a barrel for the first time since May, settling around US$109.86 on 16 October, as Iran stepped up attacks around the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi forces struck Saudi Arabia; the IEA warned diesel-market strains could persist into 2027.

items.headline: Netflix, Meta and Tesla headline a heavy week of earnings
items.summary: Netflix, Meta and Tesla lead a packed earnings week starting 19 October; Netflix reports on 20 October after cutting about 1,000 jobs, or 6% of staff, and replacing its chief content officer, with analysts expecting roughly 40% earnings growth.

items.headline: Gold holds near US$4,165 as haven demand meets a cautious Fed
items.summary: Gold held around US$4,165 an ounce on haven demand and lower yields, still well below its January record above US$5,500, as traders weighed the odds of a Federal Reserve rate decision later this month.

items.headline: Trump's Russia 'diesel deal' could hand Moscow more than money
items.summary: Analysts warned that a reported arrangement easing pressure on Russian diesel flows could aid Moscow's war effort and complicate support for Ukraine, even as it aims to cool fuel prices, CNBC reported.

items.headline: Davidovich Fokina wins the Shanghai Masters for his first Masters 1000 title
items.summary: Spain's Alejandro Davidovich Fokina fought back to beat compatriot Rafael Jodar 1-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 in the Shanghai Masters final on 18 October, claiming his first ATP Masters 1000 title and rising to a career-high No. 13.

items.headline: Jodar, 20, falls in the Shanghai final but nears an ATP Finals debut
items.summary: Rafael Jodar, the youngest Shanghai Masters finalist in the event's history, lost the final to Davidovich Fokina but stayed on course to qualify for the season-ending Nitto ATP Finals in his breakthrough year.

items.headline: India and West Indies finish their T20I series level at 2-2
items.summary: The deciding fifth T20I in Bengaluru was washed out with India 118-5 after 7.4 overs on 17 October, leaving the five-match series drawn 2-2; West Indies' Shai Hope was named Player of the Series.

items.headline: Red Bull extends team principal Laurent Mekies' contract to 2031
items.summary: Red Bull handed team principal and chief executive Laurent Mekies a contract extension through the end of 2031; he took over from Christian Horner in July 2025 and has overseen back-to-back wins for Max Verstappen in Malaysia and Singapore. The US Grand Prix in Austin is next, on 23-25 October.

items.headline: An amateur astronomer uses AI to flag a possible hidden super-Earth
items.summary: Amateur astronomer Pavel Rabtsevich, running custom AI tools on NASA's archived TESS data, found a repeating transit-like signal around the star TIC 4206066 about 116 light-years away; NASA's TESS team plans to re-examine the star in November to test whether it is a planet.

items.headline: The world is closer to a key conservation target than thought, a study finds
items.summary: A Nature study sampling 25 countries estimated that protected and conserved areas already cover about 26.81% of land, closer to the global '30% by 2030' goal than official tallies suggest.

items.headline: A blind test of methane-detecting satellites lends credibility to emissions data
items.summary: In a year-long Arizona trial of 746 events, researchers found many of 12 government, commercial and non-profit satellites accurately detected and quantified controlled methane releases, with instruments purpose-built for methane sensing performing best.

items.headline: An unprecedented atlas maps mitochondria across the tree of life
items.summary: Scientists charted the mitochondrial proteins of six organisms - five single-celled parasites and a plant - uncovering dozens of proteins absent in humans but shared among parasites that cause diseases such as malaria, and reopening debate over when the mitochondrion first evolved.

fun_fact.headline: Fresh pineapple digests the proteins in your mouth
fun_fact.body: Fresh pineapple fights back when you eat it. The fruit is loaded with bromelain, a mix of protein-digesting enzymes, so a big helping can leave your tongue, lips and the roof of your mouth feeling raw - the pineapple is literally breaking down the proteins in your mouth faster than your saliva can wash them away. The same enzyme makes pineapple a natural meat tenderiser, and because heat destroys bromelain, tinned or cooked pineapple does not bite back.
fun_fact.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica (bromelain); Royal Society of Chemistry

puzzle.title: Hands Together
puzzle.body: At exactly 3:00, a clock's hour hand points at the 3 and the minute hand points at the 12. Some time shortly after 3:00, the two hands overlap perfectly. To the nearest second, at what time does this happen?
puzzle.approach: Work out how fast each hand moves in degrees per minute, then find the moment they line up.
puzzle.answer: About 3:16:22 - precisely 3 hours and 16 and 4/11 minutes. The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute, the hour hand 0.5 degrees per minute. At 3:00 the hour hand leads by 90 degrees, so 6t = 90 + 0.5t gives 5.5t = 90, t = 180/11 = 16.36 minutes (16 min 22 sec).

word_puzzle.title: Snake in the Grass
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into four hidden groups of four: RUBY, COBRA, SWALLOW, JADE, PYTHON, WREN, VIPER, OPAL, SWIFT, ADDER, ROBIN, JAVA, PEARL, MAMBA, FINCH, CORAL. Three tempting words are not where they first appear to belong.
word_puzzle.approach: Watch for words doing double duty; one obvious member of some groups has been lured into a trickier category.
word_puzzle.answer: Snakes: COBRA, VIPER, ADDER, MAMBA. Programming languages: PYTHON, RUBY, JAVA, SWIFT. Birds: SWALLOW, ROBIN, WREN, FINCH. Gemstones: JADE, PEARL, OPAL, CORAL. The trap: PYTHON, RUBY and SWIFT read as snake, gem and bird but are all languages here.
